key_fit: not a transcription: 黑 hək (曉, -k) and 嶺 (來 qing) are Chinese words "black range"; nothing to test against the key
proposed_form: Pers. *Siyāh-kōh "black mountain" (translation equivalent, not a transcription)
attestation: Hori via Ji 1985 p. 46 (Siyahkoh range); Watters: native Siah-koh
quote: 一)黑嶺:一作黑山,堀謙德《解說西域記》頁31謂“卽波斯
note: Greek Paropamisos is no equivalent of 黑嶺 and should go: the Chinese name is a translation. Siyāh-kōh is the meaning-equivalent proposed by Hori (via Ji) and Watters. In the files the name Siyāh-koh belongs to other ranges (Minorsky, Ḥudūd comm. on §5 9Ba: the range S of the Herat river; also the Mangyshlaq "Siyah-kuh"), so it is a generic Persian range name and cannot fix this range. Watters also gives Turkic Kara Tagh. Ji's alternative: a generic name for the snowless southern ranges.

current_form: Saka Khot. Argiña; Maralbaši Saka Agñie; Niya Doc. Argiya; Toch. *Arkeñe; old 焉耆 = Argi
key_fit: 阿=a ok (影); 耆=gi ok (羣 g, 脂 i); 尼=ni ok (孃 n). No r: the key writes pre-consonantal r with a -t coda (伐 var, 達 dhar, 曷 hār), so Saka Argiña / Toch. *Arkeñe / old 焉耆 Argi MISMATCH (r unrendered)
attestation: Uighur Maitrisimit colophon, Aknidiš < Agnideśa = Yanqi (Müller, Henning, reported by Ji 1985 p. 51)
quote: Nakridiš實際上應作Aknidis(來自梵文Agnidesa),意卽爲焉耆國。
note: The characters give a-gi-ni = Skt. agni "fire", a learned Sanskritisation of local Argi/Arki (Henning; 烏夷 in Faxian), as Ji says ("阿耆尼為梵文 Agni ... 的譯音"). The Saka/Tocharian forms are the underlying local name, but XZ did not transcribe them: no r is written. The Uighur Aknidiš (Agnideśa) shows the Sanskrit name was in Buddhist use for Karashahr. Agni's -gn- cluster is written with an open 耆 (gi), not a closed character: a minor irregularity. Not checked in the Skt library for a place Agni (too common a word).

key_fit: 昭=cau (章 c, 宵 au; not in key); 怙=hu (匣; key hu 2) here for Toch. γ/k; 釐=ri/li ok (key ri 3, li 2)
attestation: Pelliot, reported by Ji 1985 p. 61 (Kuchean Cakir < Skt. cakra)
quote: 離、雀梨均爲*Čäküri, *Čöguri(<*Čökiri),*Čäkür等名的漢字不同
note: Fits Pelliot's *Čöγuri: 昭 c + au (o/ö), 怙 匣 γ + u, 釐 ri. The older 雀離/雀梨 (*tsiak-li) show the same name. Ji adds the etymology Kuchean/Agnean cakir < Skt. cakra "wheel" > "monastery". Pelliot's forms are reconstructions; no Tocharian document with the name is quoted in the files (Stein Serindia/Innermost Asia searched: nothing on the name).

key_fit: 恭=koṅ ok (見 k + -ŋ; key koṅ in 恭御陀 Koṅgoda); 御=go ok (疑 ŋ = g; key go in 恭御陀)
attestation: Kankiyāq / Kankrāq, a town on the left bank of the Chirchik one farsakh from Khudaynkath (Barthold, Turkestan p. 173; Iṣṭakhrī K.nk.rak among the towns of Shāsh, Minorsky, Ḥudūd comm. p. 357)
quote: town of Kankiaq, at a distance of one farsakh from Khudaynkath.
site_lead: Kankiyāq/Kankrāq, left bank of the Chirchik (Barthold 173); not located
note: XZ's 恭御 elsewhere renders Koṅgo- (恭御陀 Koṅgoda), so the name was *Koṅgo/*Kuŋgu. Ji puts the town among the c. 40 towns of Shāsh-Īlāq (Chirchik and Angren basins); Barthold lists them (Khatunkath, Barkush, Khargankat, Kankiyāq ...). Kankiyāq/Kankrāq on the Chirchik is the only name in the lists that begins *Kaŋk-, and it lies in the right district near Nujkath (Chirchik station). But the vowels differ (a vs o) and the -rāq of K.nk.rak is not written. Two characters: a chance match is easy. Searched Barthold and Ḥudūd town lists of Shāsh/Īlāq.

key_fit: 笯=nu/no ok (泥; XZ 奴故反); 赤=chi(k) (昌 ch + -k): Iranian č, but aspirated where j would be 常: weak point; 建=kand ok (-kand, cf. 颯秣建 Samarkand)
attestation: Nujakath, Ḥudūd §25.81 (Minorsky: near the Chirchik railway station); Nujkath, Barthold p. 174; Iṣṭakhrī Nujakath; Xin Tang shu 弩室羯
quote: 81. NUJAKATH, a borough from which come the boatmen
note: The Arabic -kath is Sogdian -kanθ, which XZ writes 建 -kand as in Samarkand; *Nujkand is therefore the Sogdian form, and the Arabic Nūjkath is attested. 赤 (昌, -k) gives a voiceless č or a č followed by k: *Nūč-kand rather than *Nūj-. The Tang 弩室羯 (*nu-ɕit-kat) agrees on -kath and has š. Ji: Nujakath/Nujikath/Nujkath, "new town". Not checked against Sogdian documents (none in files).

key_fit: 葉 single character: 以 y- + -p (or 書 ś- + -p; key śya 2 in kāśyapa); renders at most *yap/*yaγ- as an abbreviation
attestation: Marquart, reported by Ji 1985 pp. 83–84: MP *jaxšarta; the Ḥudūd and Barthold call the Syr Darya Khashart
quote: 馬迦特考證,藥殺水當是中世波斯語(Pahlavi)*jaxšarta 或 *jaxša-
note: One character, so the test is empty: any name in y- fits. The Life has 葉葉河 (perhaps a corruption of 素葉, Ji p. 83 note), the Tang 藥殺 (*jak-ʂɛt) renders the full Yaxšart. Khashart (Ḥudūd §25.81, Barthold p. 174: "Khashart (Yaksart, i.e. Syr-Darya)") is the Islamic form of the same name. 葉 may abbreviate *Yaxš-.

current_form: Skt. sutṛṣṇa (?); Arab. Usrūshana, Surūshna, Sutrūshna; Iran. *surūshna
key_fit: 窣=su(t) ok (s, u-coloured; 窣堵 = stu/sutu); 堵=tu ok (端); 利=ri/ru (來); 瑟=ṣ ok as š (生, closed C1 before n; Iranian š = 生 as in 羯霜那, 屈霜你迦); 那=na ok
attestation: Arabic forms Sutrūshnah, Surūshnah, Usrūshanah (Le Strange p. 474); Sutrūshana preferred by Minorsky (Ḥudūd p. 354) per Ji; Barthold "Ushrusana or Sutrūshana"; Sui 蘇對沙那, Tang 率都沙那
quote: also written Usrushanah, Surush- nah and Sutrhshnah
note: The characters write s-t-r-š-n: only the Sutrūšna variant has the t (Surūshna and Usrūshana lack it), and XZ's 瑟 before 那 gives the cluster -šn- of Sutrūšna. Mizutani's "Skt. sutṛṣṇa" is a pseudo-Sanskrit reading and should go; Ji's "Sutrena, dry" is likewise unsupported. Ji cites Minorsky that Sutrūshana is the better transcription, confirmed by the Chinese forms. Minorsky himself (Ḥudūd comm. p. 354) favours *Surushna in the file I have: the t-form is Le Strange's and Barthold's variant. | Confidence lowered to medium in review: only Le Strange and Barthold give the t-form; Minorsky prefers *Surushna, and 窣's -t coda could itself render r.

key_fit: 赤=čaγ (昌 ch for Iranian č + -k for γ); 鄂=γā/ŋā (疑 + -k): Iranian γ, not Indic; 衍=ya(n) ok, 那=na ok (-衍那 = -iyān regular). The -ni- of -niyān is not written
attestation: Ḥudūd §25.25, 27 CHAGHANIYAN; Le Strange p. 435 Saghaniyan = Pers. Chaghaniyan; Marquart: XZ's form a transcription of NPers. Čaγā[ni]yān
quote: Hūan-čuangs Tsik-gok-jan-na ist eine unvollkommene Transskription für skt. * Caghà[ni]-
note: The current label "Altpers." is wrong: Čaγāniyān is the New Persian/Arabic form (Marquart: XZ's transcriptions already reflect the NPers. forms, not MP *Čak-ān-īk-ān). XZ writes *Čaγāyān(a): the syllable -ni- is missing, as -dhi- is in 鞠和衍那 (Marquart). Tang 支汗那/石汗那 render the short form Čaγān. The non-Indic values (赤 ch for č, 疑 for γ) have precedents in 赭時 Chāch and 喝捍 Kharghān.

key_fit: 鞠=kub ok (見 + -k; key kub, kubja); 和=wā (匣合 ɣw for w; Iranian value); 衍=ya(n) ok, 那=na ok; -dh- (-dhi-) not written
attestation: Barthold p. 72 Quwadhiyan; Ḥudūd §5.11 and index Qavādiyān (Qubādhiyān); Le Strange p. 440 Kubādhiyān; Marquart p. 226 n. 1
quote: days from Quwadhiyan, probably on the site of the present town
site_lead: Qabadian / Kobadian on the lower Kafirnihan
note: Kub-wā-yāna = Qub/Quwādhiyān with the -dhi- syllable unexpressed (Marquart: "Kio-ho-jen-na = skt. *Kuwa[dhi]jāna"). 鞠's -k coda renders b as in the key's kubja, so both Qubādh- and Quwādh- are written. The Tang 久越得健 / 俱德健 (Ji) render a -kand form. Mizutani's "*Kuwayāna" is right as a reading of the characters but should be labelled as XZ's form of Quwādhiyān.

key_fit: 鋭=yu/ywi (以 y-, MC jwiej; not in mc.tsv); 秣=mar/mat (明 + -t; Iranian mar/mur as in 颯秣建, 弭秣賀); 陀=d/dh (定)
attestation: Marquart, Ērānšahr p. 227 (an Arabic district name, garbled in the OCR), reported by Ji 1985 p. 125
quote: 銳秣陁國:馬迦特認為銳秣陁爲 Zumathān 之對音,
note: Zumathān fits 秣陀 = -math- and the position S of the Oxus on the Hindu Kush slopes, but 以 y- for z breaks the key (z = 習/寔; the only precedent is the "odd" 以 for š in 愉漫 Shumān), and the final -ān is not written. The Arabic word is unreadable in the Eranshahr OCR (line 13628, "آلرمثان", i.e. al-R/Zumathān?), so I could not check Marquart's reading. No form like *Yumar-/*Zumar- found in the Ḥudūd, Barthold or Le Strange. Mizutani's *Yumadha is the literal reading. Sar-i-pul (the map point) has no support from the name.

attestation: Ḥudūd §23.78 BAMIYAN; MP Bāmīkān (Bundahišn, Marquart); Marquart: Fan-jen-na, old *Bam-jan-na, a Sanskritisation
quote: 78. BAMIYAN, a land on the frontier between Guzganan and the
note: Fits Bāmiyān exactly with the regular -衍那 = -yāna. As with 赤鄂衍那 and 鞠和衍那, XZ hears the (N)Pers. -iyān form, not MP Bāmīkān (-k- not written). Ji (after Pelliot) gives the same derivation. The older 范陽 / 帆延 / 望衍 are other renderings (Ji).

key_fit: 阿=a ok; 路=ru/lu ok (來 模 u; key ru 2); 猱=nau (泥 + 豪 au; XZ's own fanqie 奴高反): MISMATCH for ṇa (key: ṇ = 拏, final a = 歌-rhyme 那)
note: XZ took care to fix 猱 as nau with 奴高反, so the last syllable had an au/o vowel and a dental n: aruṇa does not fit (retroflex ṇ and final a would be 拏 or 那). A vernacular ending in -o (Bactrian nominative -o, Gāndhārī -o) on *Arun- would explain 猱, but the key has no -o < -aḥ case and no *Aruno is attested. Searched the Skt library for aruṇa + giri/parvata/śaila/acala (only Aruṇagiri the person) and for ramaind/ramendu. Ji's Aruṇācala (after B.C. Law) is a Himalayan homonym. The Sūrya link (Kuwayama's Khair Khana) rests on aruṇa and weakens with it.

name_zh: 比羅娑洛山 (象堅窣堵波)
key_fit: 比=pi ok (並/幫; key pi 1); 羅=la/ra ok but MISMATCH for lu (u would be 路/盧/嚕); 娑=sā ok (心); 洛=ra(k)/la ok (key la 1, ra 1; -k coda unexplained)
attestation: Gloss 唐言象堅 fixes the meaning; Skt. pīlu "elephant" in the kośas (the Skt. word is the loan of Pers. pīl); Ji: Pers. pilu + Skt. sāra
quote: 比羅娑洛山:波斯語 pilu 意譯為象,梵語 sāra 意譯為
site_lead: Three hills S of the Koh-Daman stream (Higuchi, via Ji)
note: The gloss confirms elephant + firm. But 羅 is never lu in the key, so XZ heard *pīla-, i.e. the Iranian pīl (+ linking a), not Skt. pīlu. Library: pīlu = mataṅgaja in the kośas, e.g. various-kosas line 15954 "pīluḥ kāṇḍe tarau puṣpe paramāṇau mataṅgaje |" and Śabdaratnasamuccaya-type entry "vṛkṣajātigajau pīlū"; no compound pīlusāra/pīlasāra found (searched pilusar, pilasar: only pīlusarṣapa in medicine). The hybrid Iranian–Sanskrit name suits Kāpiśī.

key_fit: 漕=dzau (從 dz + 豪 au): MISMATCH for jā (key j = 常 23/24; 從 dz unattested in the key, fits Iranian z/dz); 矩=ku ok (key ku 3); 吒=ṭa (知, reliable voiceless retroflex): ḍ of jāguḍa would be 荼/擇, MISMATCH (voicing)
attestation: Mbh 3.48.21 jāguḍān ramaṭhān ...; Mārkaṇḍeya P. 57.40 (northern peoples, with Lampāka); kośas: jāguḍa = kuṅkuma (saffron); Ji p. 148: Jāguda "saffron"
quote: lampākāḥ śūlakārāśca cūlikā jāguḍaiḥ saha  /
note: The text says the country "宜鬱金香" (suits saffron), and Skt. jāguḍa means both a north-western people (with the Lampākas in MārkP 57.40; with the Ramaṭhas in Mbh 3.48.21) and saffron (Rājanighaṇṭu 12.39 kāleyakaṃ jāguḍaṃ; Vidagdhamādhava comm. jāguḍaṃ kuṅkumam). This attests Mizutani's basis and is strong on meaning. The characters, however, give *Dzaukuṭa: the initial dz-, the au and the voiceless ṭ all depart from the key. That suggests a local or Iranian form behind the Sanskrit one. Marquart (Ērānšahr p. 39) instead links 漕矩吒/漕利 with Zābul (Zāwul); 從 dz suits Z-, but -kuṭa does not. The name points to Foucher's Jaghuri (upper Arghandāb) as much as to Ghazni. | Verdict changed keep → doubtful in review: three mismatches with the key (dz-, au, voiceless ṭ).

key_fit: 鶴=γa(k) (匣 γ + -k; Iranian γ = 匣 as in 胡 gh); 悉=s (心, closed): Iranian z is 習/寔 elsewhere, MISMATCH for z; -k coda of 鶴 unexplained; 那=na ok
attestation: Ḥudūd §24.19 GHAZNIN (spelt Ghazaq); Marquart p. 39: Ho-si-na = Ghazn/Gazna (older *Ganzak); Pelliot (in Foucher II p. 240 n. 35): equivalence unresolved
quote: GHAZNiN (spelt: Ghazaq), 2i town situated on the slope of a
note: Ghazna gives γa-z-na, but XZ writes *γak-s-na: a voiceless s and an extra -k. Pelliot (via Foucher) reads *γâk-sĭet-nâ and calls it "pas très conciliable avec Ghazna"; he notes that the Tang shu calls the second capital A-so-ni and that a 660 district Hao-sa-ta used a near-homophone of 鶴. No better form found. The Ghazni identification rests on the route fit and the Tang shu, not on the name.

key_fit: 鶴=γa(k) (匣 + -k); 薩=sa(t)/sar (心 + -t; key s 3, sar 2); 羅=ra/la
quote: tale, Hao-sa-lo est *yāk-sât-lâ, mais est appelée A-so-ni
note: Mizutani's *ghasala is a literal reading; with 薩's -t for r the form could be *γasra/*γasar. Pelliot (in Foucher) gives *γâk-sât-lâ and notes the Tang shu name A-so-ni (*Asani), which differs. Cunningham's Guzar (Ozola) is a vague modern name not in my files. Searched Ḥudūd, Le Strange and Barthold for Ghazar/Guzar/Hazar- near Zābulistān: nothing. Three characters, partly shared with 鶴悉那.

key_fit: 羅=ra/la; 摩=ma ok; 印=in (影, -n; key in 1): a mid-name 印 signals a vowel-initial member (key §5); 度=du/dhu ok (定 模)
quote: He spells the name Hindmand, Hidmand being a common variant
note: No form found. Searched the Skt library for ramaind, ramendu, lamaind (only mantra and astrological compounds) and the Iranian files for Rāmīd/Rāmand: Barthold's Rāmīdh is the Kafirnihan (Mizutani's doubt), far away. The Islamic Helmand spellings Hindmand/Hidmand/Hirmand (Le Strange p. 339) share the *ind- of 印度 but not in this order. XZ's 印度 is also his own spelling of "India" (indu), so 羅摩印度 may be a half-translated or folk-etymological name ("Rāma's India"?). The Helmand identification rests on geography only.

key_fit: 護=hu (匣 模; key hu 2 for 怙); 苾=bi(t) (並 b + -t): b where Hupiān has p (p = 幫), weak MISMATCH; 那=na ok
attestation: Foucher I p. 136: Hopiân, NW of Charikar; Foucher cites Stephanus' Opianē
quote: testablement très ancien de Hopiân, à une petite lieue au Nord-Ouest de Charikâr.
note: Hu-bi-na fits Hupiān/Opiān except for the voiced 苾 (p would be 幫), which non-Indic names allow (b/p are not always kept apart outside the key). Majumdar is right that 護 is no K-, so Cunningham's Kophene/Kipin fails. The ancient Opianē (Stephanus, via Foucher) shows the name is old. The name fits; whether the capital of 12.02 lay so far north is the separate route question (Foucher).

key_fit: 安=an (影 + -n) ok; 呾=t (端, closed C1 of tr, key 呾羅 = tra 13×): t where Andarāb has d, MISMATCH (d = 達/陀); 羅=ra ok; 縛=ba/va ok (Iranian b, cf. 縛喝)
attestation: Ps.-Moses Xorenacʿi, Arm. Andrap = Andarāb (Marquart, Ērānšahr p. 81); Ḥudūd §23.77, 80 Andarāb
quote: Mit Andrap kann nur Andaräb
note: Read with the key's cluster rule, 安·呾羅·縛 is an-trā-b(a), a three-syllable *Andrāb with a d-r cluster, not Mizutani's four-syllable *antarava. The Armenian Andrap shows exactly that cluster; Arabic Andarāb has the anaptyctic a. The only departure is 呾 t for d after n, and Armenian p for b shows that voicing wavers in this name. The Iranian name is secure; only the label changes.

key_fit: 闊=khwa (溪合 kʰw + -t): Iranian x is 曉 elsewhere (喝, 貨, 忽), so 溪 for x is a MISMATCH but w is rendered; 悉=s (心, closed C1 of st); 多=ta ok
proposed_form: Xwast / Khwāst (Pers.; Arm. West); mod. Khost
attestation: Marquart, Ērānšahr p. 81: Ps.-Moses West = Pers. Xwast or Xust, the Kʿwoh-si-to of XZ; Ḥudūd comm. p. 341: Khost valley
quote: Zur Wiedergabe von pers. Xwast
note: Khwa-s-ta writes the cluster -st- in the key's way (closed s character + ta) and keeps the w that the Persian spellings خواست Xwāst show. *Khasta loses the w. Final -a is either a Sanskritising vowel or the open 多. Xuanzang uses 溪 here where he usually uses 曉 for Iranian x.

current_form: Iran. *γwar (OCR *rwar); 遏換/阿緩 of the Tang shu
key_fit: 活=ɣwat (匣合 ɣw + -t; also 見 kwat): ɣw for Iranian w as in 和 = wā (鞠和衍那), -t coda for r (Iranian practice: 秣 mar, 呾 tar)
attestation: Marquart, Ērānšahr p. 85: Hwo and Tang 阿緩 *Awan = *War/Awar, the base of Arab.-Pers. Warwālīz (Valvālij of the Ḥudūd §23.73, = Kunduz); Bactrian Warnu (Sims-Williams), reported, not in files
quote: wovon die arabisch-persische Form Warwālīz eine Verdoppelung wäre
note: The γ of *γwar is the Chinese initial for w (cf. 和 = wā), so the name XZ heard is *War. Marquart derives Warwālīz from *War by reduplication and suffix, and links it with the Tang 阿緩. Sims-Williams' Bactrian documents name a town Warnu (ουαρνο), identified with Warwālīz and 活 (reported, not in files). That makes it a near-certain match, but I cannot quote it, so confidence is medium. Marquart's Avar etymology is speculative and not needed. This firms the Kunduz identification (01.28a, 12.05), which the notes call "not continuous with Kunduz".

key_fit: 瞢=muṅ/məṅ (明 + -ŋ; -ŋ before a velar, key §4); 健=gān ok (羣; Iranian -gān = 健 as in 胡寔健, 呾剌健)
attestation: Marquart, Ērānšahr p. 226 (Mung-kien; Bīrūnī's Canon: Mundajān); Ḥudūd comm. p. 367: Munjān (Mundajān; Sanglichi Mandežān)
quote: aber, wie Vos zeigt, nicht einfach mit dem heutigen Mungan oder Mungan, einem
note: Mungān fits both characters exactly. The modern district of that name lies far up the Kokcha in Badakhshan. Marquart (following Yule) and Ji keep the name but extend the old district down the Bangi valley to the Tāliqān and Khānābād plains, which saves the route. The name supports Beal/Vivien's Munjān (or Marquart's larger district), not a point near Khanabad. Mizutani's "no matching place name" is not right: the match is Mungān/Munjān, and the open question is its old extent.
